children.text: A tiered waterfall in a limestone canyon in Badian, southwest Cebu, with an overwhelming turquoise color tinged with milky white. You can either walk in to see just the first-level falls, or do canyoneering — jumping and swimming down from the upper canyon — and the latter is considered a highlight of any Cebu trip.
Kawasan Falls is a canyon waterfall in Barangay Matutinao, in the municipality of Badian, about

southwest of Cebu City. Because of the lime dissolved in water flowing through limestone country, the water takes on a turquoise color that looks as if a little milk has been stirred in, and in the sunlit morning the real thing feels even more surreal than the photos. The falls continue in several tiers, and the largest and most famous is the first-level (main) falls, close to the entrance.

The falls are a multi-tiered cascade that runs down into three large pools. Water that begins at the Kabukalan spring flows through the Kawasan canyon and along the Matutinao River into the Tañon Strait. On-site signboards state that the river was named the cleanest river in the country in

and inducted into the Hall of Fame, and that it is home to Philippine long-tailed macaques, fruit bats, dragonflies and butterflies endemic to Kawasan, and the Cebu-endemic bird siloy. Reports say Badian draws about 1,000 visitors a day and that tourism revenue reached about
in
; with that much popularity, reservation, guide, and life vest rules are now tightly managed.
There are broadly two ways to enjoy Kawasan. The first is to walk about
15–20 minutes

through the forest from the roadside entrance to the first-level falls, then swim and ride a bamboo raft. The second is canyoneering, starting from the upper canyon in neighboring Alegria and spending about
3–5 hours
walking, swimming, and jumping off rocks along the gorge all the way down to Kawasan Falls. Most travelers choose canyoneering, and it's often cited in Cebu trip reviews as 'the most memorable day.'

The canyoneering course is accompanied by a professional guide, and you wear a helmet and life vest, so you can join even if you're not a strong swimmer. Most jump points have a bypass route, so if you're scared, you can walk down or slide down instead. Still, since you'll be climbing over rocks and pushing through currents for several hours, basic fitness is required.
It's about
30 minutes

by car from Moalboal, so pairing it with a Moalboal stay is the most efficient option; from Cebu City or Mactan, many take a dawn-departure day tour combining it with the Oslob whale sharks. It's recommended for adventurous young travelers, groups of friends or colleagues, and families with enough stamina alike.

A route starting from the upper canyon on the Alegria side, walking and swimming down the gorge all the way to Kawasan's first-level falls. Guides often help with waterproof bags and action cam footage, so you can also take home a video keepsake.
Along the route you jump from rocks several meters high into turquoise pools. The highest jump point is said to be around
, and all jumps are optional.
Swim in the wide pool beneath Kawasan's largest falls. Life vests are mandatory, and it's popular to sit on the rocks under the waterfall's flow for photos.
Ride a bamboo raft under the first-level falls right up to the base of the waterfall's flow for a 'water bomb massage.' Check on-site whether it's operating and the fee.

blocks.title: Visit the second and third-level falls

children.text: The upper falls above the first level have fewer crowds and clearer water. General visitor access may currently be limited, so passing through on the canyoneering course is the surest way to see them.
Some operators let you add a zipline crossing the canyon before or after canyoneering. It's a thrilling experience looking down over the whole gorge.

blocks.title: Lunch at a stall by the falls

children.text: Have lunch and rest at the stalls and restaurants beside the falls, with grilled chicken, grilled fish, and rice. A policy restricting outside food was announced after the 2023 reopening, so follow the on-site instructions. Canyoneering packages often include lunch.

The canyoneering section has natural slides where you slip down between the rocks, and a section where you swim through a dark cave hung with stalactites. The jumps are graded from low spots up to the highest one, so you can warm up on a low one at first.

Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) is the closest. Direct flights from Incheon and Busan take about
4 hours 30 minutes

1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila. From the airport to Badian takes about
3–4 hours
by car.

3 hours 30 minutes–4 hours

In Moalboal, motorbike rental costs about
a day, and riding south along the coastal highway for about
30–45 minutes
brings you to Matutinao. By private car from Cebu City, the west coast highway through
Carcar

The dry season from
December
to
May
is best. Low rainfall keeps the canyon water a clear turquoise, and canyoneering operates reliably. In
March–May
, strong sunlight makes the water color look most vivid, but crowds are heavier too.
During the rainy season,
June–November
, the canyon water turns muddy after rain and water levels rise sharply, so canyoneering can be suspended for a day or two. During typhoon season (mainly
August–November

), the falls themselves are sometimes closed. If visiting in the rainy season, be sure to check whether it rained the day before and whether the operator is running normally. On weekends and during the Easter and Christmas holidays, local visitor numbers rise sharply, so an early morning visit is recommended.
After Typhoon Odette badly damaged the canyon in
December 2021
, Cebu Province temporarily closed the falls in
June 2023
to remove hazardous structures and clear out unlicensed canyoneering operators, and reopened them in
October 2023
after improvements including guide training. In
June 2026
, the province handed Badian a repair budget of

to clear the rocks and sediment that Typhoon Tino and others had washed onto the riverbed and to improve safety facilities. The governor said the work would be done zone by zone without closing the falls, so that tourism and residents' livelihoods would not be disrupted.
On
October 23, 2025
, a falling rock in the Matutinao gorge injured a guide, and the Badian local government paused canyoneering from
October 26
and resumed it on
October 28
(the falls stayed open). After Typhoon Tino (international name Kalmaegi) passed over Cebu on
November 4
, both Kawasan Falls and canyoneering were closed as of
November 6
while cleanup continued. Suspensions after heavy rain are frequent beyond this too, with others in early
April 2025
and on
June 22
(resumed the next day), so even in the dry season, leave slack in your schedule and check local government and operator announcements.

There are small resorts and guesthouses near the falls entrance too, but most travelers stay in Panagsama, Moalboal, about
30 minutes
away by car. Panagsama offers a wide range of options at about
a night and is convenient with restaurants and dive shops clustered together. If you want a quiet retreat, there are also upscale resorts along the Badian coast, running
or more a night.

Restaurants and stalls around the falls sell simple Filipino food such as chicken and pork barbecue, grilled fish, pancit (stir-fried noodles), and rice. After the 2023 reopening, a policy was announced that food may be sold only at designated stalls and that outside food is restricted, so check the on-site rules. After canyoneering you'll be so worn out that anything tastes good. Back in Moalboal you can enjoy seafood barbecue and a variety of international cuisines. There is said to be a snack stall at a rest stop along the course, but this isn't guaranteed, so put water and an energy bar in a waterproof bag before you set off.

Choose where to stay according to your plans. Panagsama in Moalboal, with its restaurants, dive shops, and money changers, is the most convenient; to start your morning right at the falls, accommodations around Lambug Beach on the Badian coast are close. If you're combining it with the Oslob whale sharks, you can also stay in Oslob and visit Badian as a day trip. Badian is a town famous for banig, a traditional woven mat, so you can buy handicrafts such as mats and bags as souvenirs.
Most canyoneering trips depart between
6 and 8 AM
. The earlier you start, the quieter the canyon and the fewer people at the falls.
Aqua shoes or trekking sandals with good grip are better than sneakers. Flip-flops are absolutely not allowed.
Put your phone in a waterproof pouch and leave valuables at your accommodation. Guides often carry a waterproof bag for you.
A guide tip isn't mandatory, but many give around
per person.
Canyoneering has a fixed rate set by the Badian local government, so avoid touts offering prices that are too cheap or too expensive, and use a registered operator.
Entrance fees and shuttle fares are often cash-only, and there's no ATM on site.
For photos, shoot from the rocks on the right of the first-level falls to capture the whole waterfall together with the turquoise pool. The light is best between
9 and 11 AM
Canyoneering departures cluster between
6 and 8 AM
, the last departure is around
2 PM
, and the last entry for walk-in visitors is said to be around
3 PM
. Times can change, so check with the operator.

Cebu Province has been requiring online reservations for southern attractions, and going through an operator means they book for you. If you go on your own, entry may be difficult without a reservation in peak season (March–May and holidays), and in the rainy season also check for suspension announcements.
The
entrance fee covers 3 hours at the first-level falls, and life vests are mandatory when swimming. There's no ATM on site, so bring plenty of cash.
Life vests are mandatory when swimming at the first-level falls, and unauthorized cliff jumping at the main falls is prohibited.
Only jump at the points and in the manner designated by the guide during canyoneering, and never take part after drinking.
After heavy rain there's a risk of flash floods and falling rocks, so follow the operator's advice if they recommend suspending the trip.
Moss-covered rocks are very slippery, and ankle injuries are common. Walk slowly and keep your hands free.
Age limits (roughly 7–10 years and up) and health requirements vary by operator, so check in advance if bringing children.
Local media reported that the regulated canyoneering fee rose from
to
per person when the falls reopened in
October 2023
, but some guides still list the old fee. The falls have stayed open during the repair works, but fees, routes, and open zones may change, so check the latest conditions with a registered operator.
The day after rain, Kawasan's water turns murky and dangerous. During the rainy season, keep your schedule flexible and always check whether it's operating that day.
